note: The chat-app track of Answers Over Time: the owner asks each app BY HAND and imports the replies from a file (cli archive-chatbot-template, cli archive-chatbot-import). No software ever contacts these apps. The questions below are this track's own list: it is not linked to archive_questions.json or archive_trending.json. Every prompt is prompt_prefix, a blank line, then the question. Until the first real import the list may be changed; after it a recorded question never changes or disappears and new ones are appended. A question may carry "list": "trending": a newer question picked from what people are searching for and added along the way. The site lists those under its Trending tab and the others on the front page; cli archive-chatbot-ask --list trending asks only them. The mark only decides where a question is listed: it is not part of what is recorded about the question, so it can be added to a question that is already recorded. No politics (a crude word check refuses obvious ones). `groups` lists the kinds of place asked; a group without an answerer is shown nowhere. The group ai-models is for MODELS this software asks (cli archive-chatbot-ask, PAID class: only on the owner's word): add such an answerer to `chatbots` as {"label", "kind": "model", "name", "answerer", "group": "ai-models"} and optionally "maker", where `answerer` is a label of LIVE_ARCHIVE_MODELS and `name` says which model is asked; a name that holds a chat app's name is refused, so an answer a model gave over an API never sits under an app's name. An app entry has no `kind`, and no software ever contacts an app. A chat app names its group with `group` and belongs to the first group when it names none; a later group is added here, with its apps, and starts as new columns from its first month. Every group is asked the same questions. `human` words the column of answers written by people, which the owner collects by hand. `aside` is one line of the owner's own, shown once on the chat-app method page and never on a card; it is a joke, not a claim. Names are used only to say which app was asked; this project is not affiliated with their makers.
